## Motivation

Experimentation knowledge is weirdly tribal: every organization rediscovers the same hard lessons — peeking, underpowered tests, metric collisions — and most write-ups are either academic or vendor marketing. I want the reference I wish existed when I was learning: practical, opinionated, and honest about tradeoffs.

This will collect and expand on ideas from my post [Optimization Is a Product, Not a Project](/posts/optimization-is-a-product.qmd) — the playbook is the "how" to that post's "why."

## Scope

- **Before the test** — hypothesis writing, power analysis, metric selection, guardrails.
- **During the test** — stopping rules, peeking (and why dashboards lie), ramping.
- **After the test** — honest readouts, failed tests that were worth running, and when *not* to A/B test at all.
- **The system around it** — velocity metrics, review cadence, and the org design that makes all of it stick.

Each section gets a worked example with real-ish numbers — the plan is to generate realistic synthetic data so examples are reproducible without leaking anything confidential.

## Status & roadmap

- [ ] Outline and structure locked

- [ ] Readout template

## What success looks like

Someone runs a better test because of a chapter they read here — and can cite *why* to their leadership without needing me in the room.
